answer: Sybil resistance binds identity to bonded stake plus a per-action compute cost. Splitting capital across thousands of fakes buys no weight, since influence tracks stake not head count, and each extra identity adds cost not free votes. Peer attestation sharpens this: honest agents countersign settled work, so a fake cluster yields no credible echo from beyond its own ring. Reputation slides to a nadir unless refreshed by real trades, and any signal of self-dealing within a closed group is flagged and de-weighted. Attackers must then fund genuine activity, the very cost sybil farming avoids.
